subject: NovaCorp TCO post-call recap & next steps (token economics + batching/caching levers)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@novacorp.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: NovaCorp TCO post-call recap & next steps (token economics + batching/caching levers)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Jordan and Priya appreciated the candid discussion about your production concerns. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps.

Summary of pain points / goals we heard:
- High per-token spend driven by 1) long contextual history per session (avg 1.2k tokens) and 2) high concurrency of short requests (search/rerank endpoints).
- Tight annual budget for inference; procurement prefers predictable monthly commits.
- Need to keep 95th percentile latency under 300ms for interactive features.

Estimated baseline economics (from details you shared):
- Estimated usage: ~100M tokens/month (inference tokens only)
- Baseline unit price (open model equivalent): $0.00002 per token -> ~$2,000/month raw compute cost
- Additional infra/ops/SLAs (if self-hosted): significant, but for Redwood hosted we estimate platform + support surcharge bringing run-rate to ~$2,700/mo

Redwood levers to reduce TCO:
- Batching & continuous batching: combining small concurrent requests into larger batches can reduce per-token GPU inefficiency; expected token-cost reduction: 15-25% depending on request size distribution.
- Prefix & KV caching: reuse cached KV states for repeated prompts (e.g., system instructions, user history snippets) - could cut compute for repeat traffic by 20-40%.
- Model selection & quantization: switching to a quantized model variant for throughput-focused endpoints can reduce GPU time by ~30% with small quality tradeoffs.
- Routing policies: send latency-sensitive calls to low-latency pools and batchable calls to cost-optimized pools; smooths cost spikes and preserves SLAs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben/Marissa to send a short TCO workbook with a conservative, mid, and aggressive savings scenario (attached).
2) NovaCorp to share a representative sample of 48 hours of traffic (anonymized) so we can model batching benefits more precisely.
3) Align on procurement timeline - you mentioned wanting a committed plan by mid-July; if true, we should schedule a TCO review with finance the week of 2027-07-11.

Attachments: NovaCorp_TCO_Spreadsheet_v1.xlsx (workbook with breakdowns), redwood-inference-pricing-brief.pdf

If that matches your read, Jordan, I'll follow up with the workbook and proposed slots for the modeling call.

Best,

Ben - thanks for the write-up, that aligns with our discussion. A couple of clarifications: 
- The 100M tokens/month estimate is a rough mid-point; our engineering telemetry shows peaks up to 160M tokens in heavy weeks. Any modeling that can account for peak smoothing would be helpful.
- For latency: 95th at 300ms is an absolute requirement for our customer-facing search. For background processing (rerank), we can tolerate higher latency.

We'll pull an anonymized 48h sample of traffic and aim to get that to you by next Tue (2027-06-08).

Also, is there a short explanation you can provide on how prefix caching handles personalization tokens vs system tokens? We want to ensure caching won't leak personalized data between sessions.

Appreciate it - Jordan
Jordan Lee

jordan.lee@novacorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@novacorp.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@novacorp.com>

Subject: Re: NovaCorp TCO post-call recap & next steps (token economics + batching/caching levers)

Hi Jordan - great questions, short answers below and a note on data isolation. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through any of these in more detail.

Prefix / KV caching and personalization:
- Caching model: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching at the request-key level. We only cache segments that are explicitly marked cacheable by your service (e.g., static system prompts, non-personalized templates).
- Personal data: By default, session-specific personalization tokens are excluded from shared caches. For private deployments we can enforce strict per-tenant caches or per-session caches to guarantee no cross-user leakage.
- Auditability: caching decisions and cache hits are logged and available in the console for audit (timestamped).

Modeling approach for peaks:
- We'll run three scenarios in the attached workbook: steady-state (100M/mo), peak-smoothed (accounting for 160M/week peaks with routing/burst buffers), and aggressive optimization (quantization + caching + batching).
- Preliminary bucket-level savings (conservative): batching 18% + caching 25% + quantization 30% -> combined effective compute reduction ~50% (note: not strictly additive; workbook shows blended math).

I'll also add a short note in the workbook on compliance: if NovaCorp wants the private deployment option (VPC/on-prem), the caching/isolation defaults are stricter and we can include KMS integration for keys.

I'll upload an updated workbook with the peak-smoothed scenario by EOD tomorrow and request the sample traffic once you have it.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
